clue.text: Artist sounds happy in his work.

explanation.surface: A painter who is audibly cheerful as he goes about his job.
explanation.walkthrough: James McNeill Whistler was the American painter; the second reading is a worker who whistles as he goes, the sound of contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler is a famous painter, and one who whistles while working makes a happy noise on the job.

clue.text: Sporting event could be a flop

explanation.surface: An athletics contest might turn out to be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flop' suggests failure, but the Fosbury flop is the back-first technique used in this athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an athletics field event, and the Fosbury flop is the standard modern style of clearing its bar.

clue.text: Rides roughshod over press agencies?

explanation.surface: Someone tramples over the news agencies of the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press agencies' looks like news services, but the second reading is machines that press flat with heavy rollers.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten opposition ruthlessly is to crush it like a road machine, and those heavy machines are things that do pressing.

clue.text: Amorous rendering means nothing to Carol

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
a carol is a kind of song

explanation.surface: A romantic performance means nothing to a woman called Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' poses as a woman's name but is the festive song.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic ballad is a piece sung with amorous feeling, a performance about romance.

clue.text: Polish picture Caesar came across

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it
an icon is a religious picture or image

explanation.surface: A Polish painting that Julius Caesar happened upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the verb to shine, not the nationality. Caesar crossed this river in 49 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar famously crossed this small Italian river, starting civil war.

clue.text: Fancy being in a side at Eton

indicators.note: the letters being in the words that follow are found running across them

explanation.surface: Imagine being in a team at a famous public school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a well-known English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy, in the sense of imagine, is to form an idea in the mind.

clue.text: Document to go by

explanation.surface: A paper to proceed on the strength of.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit lets its holder through, and to overtake or move past someone is the same verb.

clue.text: Young lady is in early to leave out pound for messenger

indicators.note: the young lady is placed in the middle of the other word
the pound sign is to be left out of the word early

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl arrives early and must skip the pound before acting as courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave out' drops the pound sign, leaving EARY; 'is in' signals the container, and 'is' is not a separate link.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission carries messages on another's behalf.

clue.text: Fail to prepare adequately for such deliveries?

explanation.surface: Not getting ready properly for a certain kind of throw.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is under-equip (arm as in supply with weapons); the second is the low bowling action in cricket, with the hand below the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip with too few weapons leaves troops unready, and cricket's low bowling style has the hand kept below the shoulder.

clue.text: Old King the French regard fondly

parts.note: Og was the Old Testament king of Bashan
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch admires the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Og is a biblical king, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze amorously at someone is to look at them with desire.

clue.text: Statesman to miss out these expressions

parts.note: read as States-man, a man from the United States

indicators.note: out signals the word miss is rearranged, its letters put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician is set to drop certain turns of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' looks like a politician but splits as a man from the States; 'out' gives ISMS, a word for doctrines that also ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages peculiar to US English are phrases a man from the States would use.

clue.text: Lack of accuracy excited a unit on manoeuvres

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move around, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An excitable army unit on exercises is imprecise.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecision is a failure to be exact or correct.

clue.text: Composing eight pages is nothing after a pot of ale

indicators.note: nothing comes after the pot, so the round letter is placed last

parts.note: a quart is a measure, a pot holding two pints
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Writing eight pages is no trouble after a jug of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size made by folding a sheet twice gives four leaves, that is eight pages.

clue.text: Old English patter adapted for a musical

indicators.note: adapted means the letters are altered into a new form

explanation.surface: Antique English chatter reworked for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' turns the English letter plus the chatter into PERETTA; 'patter' is a salesman's spiel, not part of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera is a short comic musical stage work.

clue.text: Excuse for a game in gay assembly

indicators.note: the game goes in the middle of the other letters
an assembly puts parts together in a new arrangement

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A pretext for a sport at a cheerful gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' turns the cheerful word into AGY, and 'in' opens it after its first letter for the horseback sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying sorry is offering a reason or regret for a fault.

clue.text: Operating well under pressure

parts.note: read not as someone coping with stress but as a kind of well whose water rises by its own pressure

explanation.surface: Someone who performs ably when stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase describing a calm worker really describes a borehole where groundwater is pushed up without pumping.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a well taps a confined aquifer, so water flows up under natural pressure.

clue.text: Express approval of a race by a junior

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a boy is a junior male

explanation.surface: Applauding a race involving a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of encouragement or praise, like well done.

clue.text: Dimwit gets answer to clue in evening

annotationWithheld.why: Dimwit gets answer to clue in evening (8): TWIT with LIGHT (answer to clue) inside gives TWILIGHTT, nine letters; the final T would have to serve both TWIT and LIGHT
annotationWithheld.clue: Dimwit gets answer to clue in evening

clue.text: Salute CO as ordered. On the cheek?

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, as if by command

explanation.surface: A soldier salutes his commanding officer as instructed; is that cheeky?
explanation.walkthrough: CO is commanding officer; 'as ordered' rearranges SALUTE CO. The definition hints at a peck on the cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss is the formal sense, and a cheek is a common place to plant one.

clue.text: The Bells, for example, allowed as a poem

parts.note: taken as the name of a group of three performers
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Poe's work The Bells counts as verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bells' recalls Poe's poem, but here it stands as an example of a three-piece group.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short fixed form of eight lines with two rhymes and repeated lines.

clue.text: Assume control and collar the bowling

parts.note: to collar someone is to take or seize them
an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman dominates and attacks the bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'collar the bowling' is cricket slang for scoring freely, but here collar means seize and an over is six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize command of something, such as a company, is a phrasal verb of acquisition.

clue.text: Flower girl

explanation.surface: A woman who sells blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a flower-seller; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small purple bloom and also a woman's name.

clue.text: Complete diplomat should excel here

explanation.surface: A thorough envoy ought to shine in this area.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN TACT: a diplomat should excel in tact.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and undamaged is the first sense; the second is the quality of sensitivity diplomats need.

clue.text: His records should prove world-shaking

parts.note: read not as a star whose albums will be sensational but as a scientist whose readings register the earth shaking

explanation.surface: A musician whose discs are sure to be a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist studying earthquakes records tremors of the ground.

clue.text: A brief moment?

parts.note: brief read as shortened: the word for a moment written in its abbreviated form

explanation.surface: Asking about a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the short form of a word meaning a split second.

clue.text: Red flower

parts.note: Red read as Russian or Soviet, and flower as something that flows, a river

explanation.surface: A crimson bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' meant Soviet in Cold War slang; 'flower' is a crossword favourite for a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a river in Russia, flowing from the mountains of the same name to the Caspian.

clue.text: Man of taste, he — English eccentric

definitions.text: Man of taste, he — English eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A refined gentleman, who is an oddball Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges TASTE, HE and E; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur devoted to beauty and art is a person of refined sensibility.

clue.text: In dry grass aquatic creature moved unsteadily

indicators.note: the creature is put in the middle of the other word

parts.note: to ted is to spread mown grass to dry for hay
an otter is a river mammal

explanation.surface: A water animal staggered about in the hay.
explanation.walkthrough: TED, to spread grass for drying, is a farming word and a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To wobble or stagger is to walk shakily, close to falling.
